heading: What I'm Good At
aside: Pick an area. The panel shows where it was actually used.
spine: I wrote the code, supported it inside other people's organisations, and now spend most of my time where the systems meet the people who have to run them.

stages.label: Data & BI
stages.lead: Numbers somebody has to act on.

rows.label: Tencent
rows.text: Win rates, pick rates, skill effectiveness and backend telemetry, read closely enough to inform the parameters a live game was balanced on.

rows.label: AgriSentry
rows.text: Simulated weather and sensor data turned into per-crop risk alerts on the Power Platform, with a Power BI dashboard over an immutable audit trail.

rows.label: Malou Media
rows.text: 300+ candidates screened, with regular reporting on candidate sources, conversion rates and time-to-hire.

rows.label: Strategy&Ops Consultancy
rows.text: The website and learning management system of a strategy and operations consultancy, with staging, change control and documentation.

rows.label: Tasmania Student Notes
rows.text: A six-language publication with a newsroom of AI roles, specified so that a human editor approves every result before it is published.

rows.label: Malou Media
rows.text: Ran recruitment end to end, single-handed, for a 20-person organisation across content, livestreaming and operations.

stages.label: AI & Agents
stages.lead: A model answers a question. A workflow has to be safe to run.

rows.label: Qingqiu Technology
rows.text: Integrated OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude into developer workflows — system prompts, few-shot prompting, context management, model interaction logic — and built CLAW's context-processing and web features in Node.js.

rows.label: Payment & Agent Lab
rows.text: A FastAPI/SQLite payment prototype and a read-only operations copilot: normalising results from three simulated channels, event de-duplication, audit logging and a deterministic state machine.

rows.label: Perfect World · Lilith Games
rows.text: AIGC production pipelines across global live-service titles — LoRA fine-tuning, dataset curation, and training non-technical art teams to use the tools.

stages.label: Software & Web
stages.lead: Things that have to keep running after I leave.

rows.label: This site
rows.text: Next.js static export with a content layer that refuses the build when a link does not resolve, a status is invented, or a second language creeps back in. 104 tests sit behind it.

rows.label: LifeOps Atlas
rows.text: Node.js 24, TypeScript, Fastify 5 and PostgreSQL 17: one canonical database with append-only corrections, so a correction never destroys what it corrected.

rows.label: Rivulet LocalOps
rows.text: A written policy compiled into checks a decision has to pass, with every step recorded in a tamper-evident ledger and reviewed by a second person.

stages.label: Testing & Support
stages.lead: The unglamorous half, which is the half that decides whether a system survives.

rows.label: UTAS Motorsport
rows.text: Multi-lap, multi-track, sensor-fault and dynamic-obstacle tests: 8/8 scenarios and 24/24 laps passed in the final software matrix.

rows.label: Strategy&Ops Consultancy
rows.text: Staging, change control and documentation, so a change can be reviewed before it reaches the people who depend on the system.

rows.label: Peer tutoring
rows.text: One-to-one support for a classmate from a non-IT background across two units — explaining concepts and breaking requirements into steps rather than handing over answers.

stages.label: Interactive
stages.lead: Built for people who never asked for a manual.

rows.label: UE5 Financial Education
rows.text: A modular Unreal Engine 5 financial-education experience with AI-driven NPCs and a FastAPI + RAG backend.

rows.label: Little Red: Sequel
rows.text: A story-driven 3D pixel-style Unreal Engine demo, independently developed, with dark-fantasy worldbuilding and hub-based scenes.

rows.label: Inspired Mind Lab
rows.text: Setting up and testing the robots and tablets for children's STEAMM workshops, then helping the children debug their own — the fastest way to learn what an interface does to someone using it for the first time.

stages.label: Autonomy & Sim
stages.lead: Perception you have to be able to trust.

rows.label: UTAS Motorsport
rows.text: A full pipeline in CARLA, ROS 2 and RViz: virtual 40-channel LiDAR, DBSCAN cone detection, multi-frame tracking, KISS-ICP localisation, centre-path generation and path following.

rows.label: Hesai Pandar40P
rows.text: The official Hesai ROS 2 driver, built for the hardware testing that follows the simulation.

rows.label: AI Town
rows.text: A Django-based multi-agent simulation built around observation, memory and planning rather than scripted behaviour.
